A constant force `F_0` is exerted continuously on a block that is initially at rest on a horizontal surface. The change in kinetic energy of the block while the block is moved from position `x=0` to `x=50` `text(cm)` is `K_1`, and the change in kinetic energy of the block as the block is moved from `x=50` `text(cm)` to `x=100` `text(cm)` is `K_2`. How does `K_1` compare to `K_2` , and why?

A.Choice: `triangleK_2=triangleK_1` because the velocity increases by the same amount between `0` `text(cm)` to `50` `text(cm)` and between `50` `text(cm)` to `100` `text(cm)`.

B.Choice: `triangleK_2=triangleK_1` because the applied force does the same work on the block between `0` `text(cm)` to `50` `text(cm)` and between `50` `text(cm)` to `100` `text(cm)`.

C.Choice: `triangleK_2>triangleK_1` because the block is moving faster on average between `50` `text(cm)` to `100` `text(cm)` than it is between `0` `text(cm)` to `50` `text(cm)`.

D.Choice: `triangleK_2>triangleK_1` because the rate of change of kinetic energy is greater between `50` `text(cm)` to `100` `text(cm)` than it is between `0` `text(cm)` to `50` `text(cm)`.
